newsitem.title: BELGIUM: GIB chairman sees more alliances.
newsitem.headline: GIB chairman sees more alliances.

text.p: Pierre Scohier, Chairman of Belgian retail group GIB, reiterated on Tuesday the company was open to strengthening its various businesses through alliances.
GIB's units include GB and Bigg's supermarkets, the Quick fast food chain and the Brico DIY unit.

"We don't exclude anything. The moment is now. It won't be in (the year) 2000. It's now we have to decide and chose, but there are many possibilities," Scohier said. He was speaking at a news conference on the 1996 results of Belgian holding company Cobepa of which he is also chairman.
"It will be in the coming months that all will become clear," Scohier added.
Observers have speculated that French retailer Promodes, with whom GB has a buying alliance, could become a full-blown partner for the supermarket group.
Scohier said, however, there were various possible candidates, including British and American groups.
"We will have at the end of the 1990s the same problems in the retail sector that we had in industry in the 1970s and 80s. That means that certain types of companies have to be huge," Scohier said.
"Groups are already forming in Europe. If a partner accelerated this pattern we have to chose them," Scohier said.
Scohier said joint ventures or alliances would probably take place at the level of the subsidiaries themselves, which are increasingly becoming stand-alone businesses with their own management.
Scohier reiterated that Cobepa, when it decided to back restructuring at the GB supermarket chain at the beginning of the 1990s, always said the results would not be seen until 1997.
"The GB plan is a success," Scohier said. "This will be seen in 1996 results." GIB's financial year ends on March 31.
